title: Premature Use of Sentinel Values to Avoid Loop Bounds Checks
pattern: Using sentinel values inside raw arrays to terminate searches instead of explicit array length bounds checking.
why_bad: Bypassing bounds checking using sentinels invites buffer overflow vulnerabilities and memory unsafety. Modern compilers automatically optimize loop bounds checking via iterator optimization and branch prediction, rendering sentinel optimizations completely obsolete [358].
detection: Loops iterating through arrays or collections that lack index limits or bounds checking because they rely on a magic sentinel value (e.g. `0` or `-1`).
counterexample: Low-level null-terminated C-string utilities (`char*`) where sentinel-based iteration is the mandated binary API standard. `Contextual`.
fix: Use safe Rust iterators which compile down to bounds-check-free assembly under the hood.
